subject.title: fix: QueuedFileWriter silently swallows all write errors

question: Should optional QueuedFileWriter diagnostic sinks emit a bounded redacted warning/debug signal on repeated write failures, and what threshold/log level should be canonical?
rationale: The remaining change is small, but it sets operator-visible logging policy for optional diagnostics and prior PR review showed a real path/error disclosure concern with a raw `console.warn`.

options.title: Add bounded redacted signal
options.body: Keep writes non-fatal, log only after a threshold and on a rate-limited schedule, and avoid raw local paths or payload/error detail in the message.

options.title: Keep diagnostic writes silent
options.body: Treat failed optional diagnostic JSONL writes as intentionally best-effort and close the issue as not planned.

options.title: Fold into broader diagnostics policy
options.body: Leave this issue open until the diagnostic JSONL rotation/security work chooses one shared operator notification model.

recommendation.title: Add bounded redacted signal
recommendation.body: Keep writes non-fatal, log only after a threshold and on a rate-limited schedule, and avoid raw local paths or payload/error detail in the message.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the shared writer and is the strongest current-history routing candidate for the core diagnostic writer policy choice.
